normativeReferences.note: The keywords MUST, SHOULD, and MAY are interpreted per BCP 14 when they appear in all capitals.

conformance.summary: A product conforms when it implements every MUST requirement that applies to its surfaces. It should implement every applicable SHOULD requirement unless it documents a reason not to. It may implement MAY requirements as appropriate.

applicability.baseline: Applies to every agent-addressable product, regardless of surface.
applicability.conditional: Applies only when the product exposes the surface named in the requirement's `applies` field.

strengths.MUST: Mandatory for products within the requirement's scope.
strengths.SHOULD: Strongly recommended; deviation permitted only with documented rationale.
strengths.MAY: Optional; implementation adds value but is not required for conformance.

alternatives.commerce: Requirements in the Commerce section are alternative, interoperating approaches. A product that accepts agent payment conforms by implementing at least one applicable Commerce requirement.

rules.MAJOR: An existing requirement's strength is raised (for example SHOULD to MUST), a requirement is removed, or a stable identifier is reassigned.
rules.MINOR: A requirement is added, an existing strength is lowered, or a reference is updated to a newer specification.
rules.PATCH: Clarifications, editorial fixes, and link updates.

versioning.stableIdPolicy: Stable identifiers are preserved across spec versions and are the canonical way to cite a requirement.

sections.name: Discoverability
sections.summary: Help agents find the product and the files they need to read.

requirements.name: robots.txt with AI policy
requirements.summary: Declare which AI crawlers are allowed. A robots.txt that distinguishes GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, and other identified agents from broad training crawlers gives agents a clear signal about intent.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: Sitemap
requirements.summary: A /sitemap.xml lets agents list the site's main URLs without crawling every page.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: llms.txt
requirements.summary: A markdown index at the site root that summarizes the product and links to the documents agents should read first.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: llms-full.txt
requirements.summary: A single-file, ingestible version of the product documentation that fits into an agent context window in one request.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: HTTP Link response header
requirements.summary: Link headers with rel=sitemap, describedby, api-catalog, or alternate surface related resources to agents without parsing HTML.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: NLWeb schema feeds
requirements.summary: A schemamap directive in robots.txt pointing to a structured feed that describes site content in schema.org vocabulary for natural-language retrieval.
requirements.applies: Products that offer search or natural-language retrieval

sections.name: Content for agents
sections.summary: Expose content in a form models can parse without running JavaScript.

requirements.name: JSON-LD structured data
requirements.summary: Embed schema.org types such as Product, Organization, Offer, SoftwareApplication, and FAQPage as JSON-LD so models can read entity and product facts directly.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: Markdown content negotiation
requirements.summary: Respond to Accept: text/markdown with a markdown representation of the page, giving agents a cleaner and more token-efficient view of the same content.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: /index.md fallback
requirements.summary: A markdown version of the homepage served at /index.md, so the primary product page is directly fetchable as plain text.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: Speakable content markup
requirements.summary: Mark portions of a page as suitable to be read aloud by voice agents using schema.org/SpeakableSpecification.
requirements.applies: Products with content meant to be consumed by voice agents

sections.name: Capabilities
sections.summary: Declare what the product can do for agents and how to call it.

requirements.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
requirements.summary: An open JSON-RPC protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to agents over Streamable HTTP or stdio.
requirements.applies: Products that expose tools or resources to agents

requirements.name: A2A Agent Card
requirements.summary: A /.well-known/agent-card.json descriptor used for agent-to-agent discovery under the A2A protocol. The Agent Card declares identity, service endpoints, supported interfaces, skills, and security schemes.
requirements.applies: Products that expose an agent-to-agent surface

requirements.name: OpenAPI
requirements.summary: A machine-readable description of HTTP APIs. Function-calling agents use OpenAPI to understand paths, parameters, schemas, and errors.
requirements.applies: Products that expose an HTTP API

requirements.name: MCP Server Card
requirements.summary: A /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json document describing a server's name, version, transport, capabilities, authentication, and tool surface for pre-connection discovery.
requirements.applies: Products that expose an MCP server over HTTP

requirements.name: MCP Apps
requirements.summary: The MCP extension for ui:// resources (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui), letting servers return renderable HTML that hosts can embed in sandboxed iframes for confirmation, payment, or generative-UI handoffs.
requirements.applies: MCP servers that return renderable UI

requirements.name: WebMCP
requirements.summary: A browser API (navigator.modelContext) and HTML-native tool metadata that let pages expose actions as MCP-style tools to in-page agents.
requirements.applies: Products whose pages expose in-page actions to agents

requirements.name: NLWeb /ask endpoint
requirements.summary: A natural-language query endpoint that returns structured schema.org responses, designed to make any site conversational. NLWeb instances also act as MCP servers.
requirements.applies: Products that offer natural-language retrieval

requirements.name: Agent Skills
requirements.summary: SKILL.md files packaging discrete, portable agent capabilities as YAML frontmatter plus markdown instructions, with optional scripts, references, and assets.
requirements.applies: Products that ship agent-invokable skills

requirements.name: ai-plugin.json
requirements.summary: A /.well-known/ai-plugin.json manifest originally introduced for ChatGPT plugins and still used as a lightweight capability descriptor.
requirements.applies: Products that expose a plugin-style capability

sections.name: Identity & Access
sections.summary: Prove who the agent is and give it scoped, revocable access.

requirements.name: OAuth 2.0
requirements.summary: The foundation for delegated, scoped access. Publish authorization and token endpoints agents can discover.
requirements.applies: Products with user-owned resources or delegated access

requirements.name: OAuth Authorization Server Metadata
requirements.summary: A /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server or /.well-known/openid-configuration document exposing issuer, endpoints, and supported scopes.
requirements.applies: Products that run an OAuth authorization server

requirements.name: PKCE
requirements.summary: Proof Key for Code Exchange with S256. The secure pattern for native and agent OAuth flows that cannot hold a client secret.
requirements.applies: Products that accept public or agent OAuth clients

requirements.name: Web Bot Auth
requirements.summary: HTTP message signatures over agent requests, with a /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory publishing the public keys an agent operator signs with. Servers verify signatures to distinguish identified agents from unattributed traffic.
requirements.applies: baseline

requirements.name: OAuth Protected Resource
requirements.summary: A /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource document declaring which authorization servers a resource trusts, plus supported scopes and bearer methods.
requirements.applies: Products that expose OAuth-protected resources

requirements.name: API Catalog
requirements.summary: A /.well-known/api-catalog linkset describing a site's public APIs and pointing agents to OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or other descriptors.
requirements.applies: Products that expose one or more public APIs

sections.name: Commerce
sections.summary: Let agents pay, initiate checkouts, and complete purchases on behalf of their users. The requirements in this section are alternative, interoperating approaches; a conformant commerce product implements at least one.

requirements.name: x402
requirements.summary: An HTTP-native payment protocol built on the 402 Payment Required status code for inline stablecoin settlement of API calls.
requirements.applies: Products that charge for API calls or resources

requirements.name: Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)
requirements.summary: OpenAPI-backed checkout sessions that let agents drive standard e-commerce flows end to end. Maintained by OpenAI and Stripe, used by ChatGPT Instant Checkout.
requirements.applies: Products that accept agent-driven checkout

requirements.name: ACP Delegate Payment
requirements.summary: A companion flow for shared payment tokens, letting an agent pay on a user's behalf with a short-lived, cart-scoped token.
requirements.applies: Payment providers that issue delegated tokens to agents

requirements.name: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
requirements.summary: A /.well-known/ucp profile declaring services, capabilities, and payment handlers, plus an agent profile URL for two-sided capability negotiation. Co-developed by Shopify and Google.
requirements.applies: Products that expose agent-driven commerce

requirements.name: Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)
requirements.summary: An HTTP 402 + Payment authentication scheme with an OpenAPI x-payment-info extension for per-call API monetization. Submitted to the IETF as draft-httpauth-payment.
requirements.applies: Products that monetize APIs at the call level
